results.title: cleanse your soul, visit pashupati nath!
results.text: never a complete trip to Kathmandu for a hindu if you haven't visited this temple. go very early in the morning to avoid long queues.

results.title: They deserve respect
results.text: Whether it's a heritage or not, it really doesn't concern me. I wouldn't have entered if it wasn't my travel mate who wished to enter. Family of the deceased were crying, deceased was being cremated, tourist stood by the side for photos shooting and observation. Like minded people would made good guess on my further elaboration. Hence, enough said.

results.title: Stunning temple complex
results.text: wonderful temples and adjoining buildings, fascinating old peoples' retirement home (and more shrines), ghats by the river, a few shops on the way out...we hired a guide who was worth every penny

results.title: Nice Place
results.text: As we saw cremation sites on the Ganges, this place, though nice to visit, was not as great as the one in India was.  But it certainly was a pleasant site to see the temple and other buildings and the river with some cremations going on.

results.title: Beautiful
results.text: We saw a funeral service while there....very very moving. It is worth asking the holy men to have your picture taken with them, will cost a dollar

results.title: Amazing
results.text: If you want to see the burning Ghats this is the place to do it. The process is fascinating and you are not made to feel voyeuristic. Climb the steps for further walks and shrines.

results.title: Divine, versatile and worth visiting
results.text: The only temple that will not cost you a penny but truth is it should. the largest temple of Kathmandu with versatile sculptures and idols, The majestic Nondi gavi (made of brass) an excellent piece of work.

results.title: Wauw
results.text:
I saw a cremation going on, it was a special experience.
Nice place to meet the locals, true religious place.
Be careful with the monkeys they are very aggressive.

results.title: Beautiful temple
results.text: As a Hindu I was able to see the temple, but be warned if you are a non-Hindu you wont be able to go into the temple complex. you can, however, walk across the Bagmati river to see the arrays of sadhus, monkeys, religious ceremonies and deer in the forest so still worth a visit.

results.title: DO ATTEND AARTI !!
results.text: My visit to Pashupatinath was fabulous. The cremation center behind temple makes you realize about 'NOTHING WILL BE YOURS'. Darshan are comfortable with a proper system. You could also darshan Nav Graha & Balaji temple inside. TRY TO ATTEND AARTI done by Local People. I do not know its done on daily basis or it was because of Sunday. Local Aarti was done with gathering of Some around 40-50 people with Flute, Dholak & many musical instruments. You will surely feel REJUVENATING.

results.title: Confronting but well worth it
results.text:
Amazing to see such an important part of life - Death.

Is an amazing place but people should be respectful of what is going on here

results.title: Beautiful sacred temple complex of Kathmandu
results.text: Pashupatinath temple and cremation ghats is a truly amazing sight to visit. A beautiful sacred temple complex by the Bagmati  river is one of the holiest for hindu people. where on average 50 bodies a day get cremated according to hindu traditions.

results.title: beautiful
results.text: this is  a temple of special significance. we were lucky to go on dasshera, the crowds were much lesser than usual

results.title: Pashupatinath Temple
results.text: This is where the cremations are carried out in accordance with the Hindu faith.  Beware of all the street vendors trying to hook you on the way into this temple area.  From the car park we walked approximately 500 meters through "The Gauntlet" and everyone has their hand out looking to snag you.   In addition to the entry fee of another approximately US$10 each we hired a tour guide for about US$10.  His English was very good and he was well informed and showed us all around the place.  It is kind of a dreary place and while we were there we saw two cremations.  One was already burning away furiously and the other was a man's body being cleansed and then set up for cremation.  The Bagmati River flows by the site and the ashes are dumped into it at the conclusion.  The river and the surrounding area are not very clean at this place.  However, the river is treated as a sacred thing and it flows to the Ganges River in India.   I was surpised by the number of tourists and other vistors.  I am glad I saw this as I was told it is a must-see.  I agree with that but also caution to not encourage by even a little bit the people walking around trying to see you scarves, jewelry, rocks, and anything else you could imagine.  They absolutely will not take no for an answer. I finally told our guide that if he could not convince these hawkers that we were not interested it would start costing him money off his fee.  The message was received and understood and then he started interceding on our benefit.

results.title: Faith Of Religion
results.text:
For believers in Hinduism it is  must  place to be visited 
It was my second visit .I visited this temple more than 30 years back At that time the whole place was a shabby small place crowded by rudrakash mala shops sadhus and beggers 
To day it is a big complex divided i three parts for smooth flow of visitors .The whole complex is much  cleaner both outside and inside. Temple Visitors must have increased thousands time during last 30 years since i visited last time  but today the whole complex is very nicely maintained  The day I visited temple it  was crowded but  the flow of visitors was very smoth and darshan was easy without anybhassle.
 Surprisingly I could not see guides harassing visitors nor I could see beggers near the temple .May be they were so small in numbers that I could not notice them .I was told by locals that guide target foreigners .It is very bad
I saw few foreign visitors retuning disappointed as they were not allowed entry in side main temple .Only Hindus are allowed inside main temple. 
I have never seen such a big Nandi in any temple and very neatly kept with a small Nandi just in front of it  For darshan of main diety two raised platforms have been put on which 2 or 3 person may stand and have good darshan from a distance
There is provision of free distribution of small quantity of parsad 
A feeling of faith and peace is felt inside main temple complex

Rudrakash and other shops have been moved out from temple complex to away on side of main roads  
The river at the back ;the cremation place for Hindus ;was surpridingly clean without any burning body but pandas were sitting in large numbers for puja and rituals of pind-dan etc .It is  very sacred place for pind dan and and similar rituals
It is most important place to visit in Nepal

results.title: SADU HEAVEN
results.text: I've always found Pashupatinath to be a somewhat dreary place, but then, I guess watching Hindu cremations is not any ones idea of a good day out. The river looks dirty & the idea of being dumped into it after cremation is not appealing. The Sardu's live above the cremation area, on the opposite side of the river & are unique in their outlook on life. About R100-200 will get you some interesting personal photos. I believe the Sisters of Loretto have a Hospice within this complex. An item not to be missed when in Kathmandu. Mountain Monarch always takes its clients here as well as the big Stupa as part of your trekking package.

results.title: important and interesting place
results.text: although if you are not a Hindu you are restricted to some areas, you still can go (for 1000 Rps) and spend as much time as you want  on bserving the whole process of creamtion- this is uncomparable with any other experience

results.title: What an experience
results.text: First of all the entrance fee is quite high (1000 NPR if not totally mistaken). With the access you'll be confronted with loitering people offering their guidance services. The temple serves as al cremation place where the dead bodies are burnt (right side for the ordinary, left side for the wealthier humans). Monks try to make their money with and praying for you. When I was there with friends we witnessed the cremation of one of the richer peoples and were able to follow from the preparation until the first flames were ignited. Compared to our western world where cremation is done is strict privacy, and normally you cannot witness it at all, this experience is somewhat great and impressive. Also if you see the crowds of people (kids, adults, school classes). Even music was played .

results.title: Interesting place.
results.text:
We paid our 10000 rps to get in, we were hassled by guides to use their services.. But we went on alone, of course we couldn't go in the temple but the grounds around it. 
We walked for ten minutes and I felt I needed to know more about this place. So I engaged the services of a young man, 18 years old and very good English. I am glad I did as I learnt a lot about the life and death of people in Nepal. 
You will see dead bodies here, so be prepared. but I didn't feel we where intruding in the families grief..local young boys dive in looking for any metal brushed into the river off the funeral fire right under the noses of the next family.. you have to visit this place to understand the atmosphere. Beware for the fake holy men! Why would anyone give them money.. We saw a real holy man in mother Therasor's old folks home, he just prays and chants and feels no need to ask for money. 
And the monkeys are a wee bit aggressive.

results.title: More hassle than it's worth
results.text: Too many people trying to sell you a guided tour (unlike the Buddhist temples in the city where you can explore on your own).
